terms.meaning: a part of the app that runs in the user's browser rather than on the server

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for shared page parts
sections.what: Brings in the link component, React state and effect helpers, and the notification bell. Marks the file to run in the browser.
sections.why: Likely reason: the shared header and its parts need navigation links, interactive state and the notification bell.
sections.watch_out: The notification bell comes from a sibling file, so changing that file's name or export breaks this page.

sections.name: ThemeToggle
sections.title: Light and dark mode switch
sections.what: A button that flips the whole site between light and dark colors. It also writes the choice to the browser's local storage under a fixed key. On load it reads the theme already set on the page, so the label reflects the current mode.
sections.why: Lets the user pick a theme that they expect to survive page reloads. Reading the saved choice back on reload is not visible in this code, so it likely happens elsewhere.
sections.watch_out: The theme starts as light in the component's own memory until the effect runs, so the label can briefly show the wrong mode. Do not rename the storage key, or the saved choice is lost.

sections.name: ScoreBar
sections.title: Score bar display
sections.what: Shows a score from 0 to 10 as a row of filled and empty blocks, with the number beside it. The blocks use whole-number rounding and the number shows one decimal place.
sections.why: Gives a quick visual sense of a rating or match strength.
sections.watch_out: A score above about 10.5 makes the blank part of the bar negative in length, which can crash this display.

sections.name: StatusPill
sections.title: Status badge with age label
sections.what: Shows a small tag with a status word and how old it is, such as NEW, a number of days, weeks, or months. Anything under one day is NEW.
sections.why: Lets the user judge how fresh a job or application is at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Weeks are counted as 7 days and months as 30 days, so the age labels are approximate.

sections.name: NAV_LINKS
sections.title: Navigation link list
sections.what: The list of pages shown in the top navigation and in the phone menu, such as Pipeline, Profile, Applications, Contacts, Companies, Config and Settings. Both menus read from this one list.
sections.why: Keeps the desktop and phone menus identical by drawing both from one list.
sections.watch_out: Each path must match a real page address. A typo here creates a link that leads nowhere, in both menus.

sections.name: Header (part 1)
sections.title: Header setup, signed-in name and sign out
sections.what: Asks the server who is signed in and keeps that email. It also tracks whether the phone menu is open and closes it when the user clicks outside it. Defines the sign-out action, which calls the logout service and sends the browser to the login page.
sections.why: The header shows the signed-in user's short name and needs the phone menu to close on outside clicks, as a usual expectation for menus.
sections.watch_out: If the user lookup fails, errors are silently ignored, so the header shows no name and no sign-out button without any message.

sections.name: Header (part 2)
sections.title: Desktop navigation bar
sections.what: On wide screens, shows the navigation links, the theme button, the notification bell, and, when signed in, the short name and an OUT button. The Settings link is highlighted in the accent color. On small screens a second set of controls shows the theme button, the bell, and the menu button.
sections.why: Likely reason: the wide and narrow layouts are separate sets of markup, and the stylesheet chooses which one is visible.
sections.watch_out: The bell and theme button are written twice, once for each layout, so a change to one must be mirrored in the other. The short name is the part of the email before the @ sign.

sections.name: Header (part 3)
sections.title: Phone menu drop-down
sections.what: When the menu button is pressed, shows the full list of pages. If signed in, it also shows the short name and a SIGN OUT button. Choosing a page closes the menu.
sections.why: Phone screens have no room for the full navigation bar.
sections.watch_out: Closing after a choice works only because each link has its own close action. Any new kind of link in this menu needs the same action.

sections.name: Footer
sections.title: Page footer
sections.what: A thin bar at the bottom of every page showing the app name, the version number and the words serverless edition.
sections.why: Identifies the app and its version on every page.
sections.watch_out: The version text is typed by hand, so it will not update when the version changes elsewhere.

summary: Shared building blocks for the app's pages: a top bar, a footer and small display parts, based on the names in the outline.
purpose: Gives every page the same header, footer and small visual pieces so they look and behave the same across the app.
why: Likely reason: avoids copying the same header and footer code onto each page.
how: Only the import lines were provided, so the steps cannot be read. The outline names suggest the file defines a theme switch, a score bar, a status label, a list of navigation links, the header in three parts and the footer. The header includes the notification bell from a sibling file.
inputs: Not visible in the code provided.
outputs: Not visible in the code provided. Expected to be the header, footer and small display parts used on other pages.
